review.title: Winks and Wrong Turkeys
review.headline: A hugged Turkey got eggsecuted, and the quiet Floofer banked ten points.
review.summary: Round 1 went to Farm after Ellis, a Meowfia Mouser, refused to name a role and drew four throws. Round 2 was the key swing. Drew's Floofer hug made Alex's honest Turkey look like a liar, so the table threw Alex out and Drew banked 10 points as the only winner. In round 3 Blair winked the score leader Drew, and a muddled Tit/Owl argument sent the table onto Ellis, a truthful Farm Owl. Drew still won the game on 14.

rounds.recap: Ellis (Mouser) dodged giving a role all day. Four players converged on him. He winked Casey, but her throw still counted, and Ellis was eggsecuted. Farm won. Alex banked 4 and most others threw Wilds or low cards, so scores stayed low.

Drew (Floofer) hugged Alex, so the Turkey gained nothing from visits by Blair and Drew. Alex's honest +0 looked like a lie, and everyone but Alex threw at him. Alex was Farm, so Meowfia won. Drew was the only cat and banked 10 points.

Blair (Mouser) winked Drew on beat 1. Casey (Sphinx) falsely claimed Tit. A confused argument over Tit guesses and Owl turned the table onto Ellis, who was telling the truth. Ellis was eggsecuted and the two cats won, but not by enough to catch Drew.

highlights.text: Ellis threw four big cards at Alex to force a tie that would eggsecute a Farm player. The other throws were too many, so it failed.
Drew's hug silently turned the true Turkey's +0 into evidence of a lie. The table threw at Alex and Drew took 10 points.
Blair winked the score leader Drew on beat 1, and Meowfia then steered the vote onto a truthful Owl.
Ellis's Owl report of a Mouser visit was true and checkable, but the table ignored it because of a shaky Tit argument.

confusions.what: Said a confused report might still be useful, then took Casey's Sphinx-visit as proof against Blair. Casey's report only showed a Sphinx visited, not that Blair was the Sphinx.
Insisted nobody visited him because his tokens were +0. He did not consider that a hug stops the Turkey's effect while still counting the visits.
Treated Alex's +0 as proof the Turkey claim was false. The hug was never considered as an explanation.
Said Alex's Turkey should have gained from her visit. She did not allow that Alex might have been hugged.

Said Casey's +0 proved Ellis wasn't Owl. A Tit with a correct guess would gain an egg, so +0 only shows Casey's guess was wrong or Casey isn't Tit. The logic was close, but Alex then used it to call Ellis a liar.
Argued Casey's +0 meant Casey wasn't Tit, then had to retract when Finley pointed out a wrong guess also gives 0.
Claimed Tit and said a guess of Owl on Ellis got no egg. This did not match what a Sphinx would have, and Ellis's Owl claim became hard to disprove.
Said Alex's Turkey should have paid out to Blair's visit, though the report on Alex shows no hug or tokens either way.

worked: The Wink gave round 1 and round 3 sharp moments. Ellis tried to cut votes by killing Casey, and Blair killed the leader on beat 1.
The Floofer hug in round 2 created a believable false story. A true Turkey with +0 plus visit claims looked like a lie. This is a fair, deduction-rich trick.
The consolation rule and the throw-count signal gave real decisions. Ellis's four-card throw at Alex in round 1 was a clever tie attempt.
Ties going to Meowfia gave the cats a real reason to throw at Farm players.
problems: Dead players still throw, so Wink barely lowers the vote count. Casey was winked but her Wild still landed on Ellis. Consider making Wink more costly to answer, or letting dead throws not count as cards for score.
The runaway lead of 10 points in round 2 decided the game. One cat banking a full round on a few mid cards made rounds 1 and 3 irrelevant. Consider capping banked value or giving Farm more upside.
Hug, Turkey and Pigeon effects are hard to read from tokens. Hugged Turkey shows +0 with no notice, so the honest player is punished. Consider telling a hugged player that they were hugged.
Most players throw Wilds and low cards, so round 1 and 3 scores were tiny. Throwing small removes the risk and the reward of a bet.

Players kept ignoring checkable evidence, such as Ellis's true Mouser visit report in round 3, and chased weak Tit/Turkey logic. Pushing a mass vote on whoever stays quiet or confusing makes the game feel like a pile-on rather than deduction.
